BiblicalUsage: Yâvên is the miry clay, the deep mire where there is no standing. The psalmist says God brought him up out of the horrible pit and set his feet upon a rock, but in the other psalm he sinks in deep mire and the floods overflow him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God lifts men out of the mire, and the rock He sets them on is Himself.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
